==English==
{{wp}}
{{rfc|en|Translations not matching with senses}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peth₂-}}
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:-<ety:bor<fro:peticiun>>}}
From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|peticiun}}, from stem of {{der|en|la|petitio|petitio, petitionem|a request, solicitation}}, from {{m|la|peto|petere|to require, seek, go forward}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/pəˈtɪʃ.ən/}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-petition.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L227565}}
{{en-noun}}

# A [[formal]] [[written]] [[request]] made by an [[individual]] or a [[group]] of people to a [[sovereign]] or [[political]] [[authority]], often containing many signatures, soliciting some [[grace]], [[right]], [[mercy]], or the [[redress]] of some [[wrong]] or [[grievance]]. {{defdate|from early 15th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|suit|q1=formal}}
#: {{ux|en|We're looking to get 10,000 people to sign the '''petition''' to have the bird colony given legal protection.}}
# {{lb|en|law|by extension}} A [[formal]] written application made to a [[magistrate]] or [[court]] for an [[order]] or a [[suit]] for [[divorce]]. {{defdate|from 1730s}}
# A [[prayer]] or [[supplication]], especially of which is [[formal]] or [[humble]] and made to a [[deity]], a [[sovereign]], or an [[authority]]. {{defdate|from c. 1330}}
#: {{ux|en|a '''petition''' to aid}}
#: {{ux|en|a '''petition''' to God for courage and strength}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|1 Maccabees|7|37|passage=A house of prayer and '''petition''' for thy people.}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make a [[petition#Noun|petition]] to (a sovereign or political authority).
#: {{ux|en|The villagers '''petitioned''' the council to demolish the dangerous building.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1955|month=April|title=Notes and News: Restoring the Festiniog Railway|journal=Railway Magazine|page=288|text=The company, appreciating the crippling affect {{sic}} that this scheme will have on its activities unless the railway is diverted, has '''petitioned''' against the North Wales Hydro-Electric Power Bill at present before the House of Lords.}}
